en.title: Diablo 4 Devs React to Netflix Show: 'Hell Yes!' to More Story
en.summary: The creative minds behind Diablo 4 are thrilled about the upcoming Netflix animated series, seeing it as a massive opportunity to expand the beloved franchise's narrative. Developers express immense excitement for the show, even more than other major game announcements.
en.body:
The dark realms of Sanctuary are expanding beyond the screen and into our streaming queues. Blizzard Entertainment has officially announced that a new animated series set in the world of **Diablo** is in development with Netflix. This news, revealed during the BlizzCon 2026 Opening Ceremony, has sent ripples of excitement through the gaming community and, perhaps even more so, through the **Diablo 4** development team itself.

**Diablo 4** Game Director **Brent Gibson** and Season Lead **Owen Leach** shared their enthusiastic reactions to the series announcement. For **Gibson**, who identifies as a "story guy," the prospect of more **Diablo** narrative is the most compelling aspect. "Even though I have no information and can't share anything, the fact that we're getting a show [is what I’m most excited about]," he stated. "I want to see more story, as much story as you can get. ... I think **Diablo's** a perfect world to start telling those stories, so I couldn't be more happy that we're getting a show."

## Sanctuary's Story Unfolds on Netflix

This isn't the first time Blizzard has explored expanding its IPs into other media, but the **Diablo** universe, with its rich lore and compelling characters, seems particularly ripe for adaptation. The developers are eager to see how Netflix will bring the gothic horror and demonic struggles of Sanctuary to life for a global audience. **Owen Leach** echoed **Gibson's** excitement, framing the show as a personal fan desire. "The show is my fan answer [for what I’m most excited about]," he admitted. "I've seen animated shows on Netflix and I'm like, ‘Hell yes.’" The hope is that this series will capture the essence of the franchise and potentially create a significant positive impact, akin to the recent success of other video game adaptations.

## A New Era for the Hellspawn

The announcement comes at a time of significant expansion for the **Diablo** franchise. Alongside the Netflix series, BlizzCon 2026 also teased **Diablo V** (slated for Spring 2029), the **Amazon class pack** for **Diablo IV** arriving in 2027, and the confirmation that **Diablo IV** will be available on the Nintendo Switch 2. The development team sees the Netflix series as a crucial piece of this evolving ecosystem, a way to deepen player engagement and attract new fans to the world of **Diablo**. They are actively involved in the process, working to find the right creative team to translate the game's dark fantasy into a compelling visual narrative.

## What's Next

While specific details about the **Diablo** Netflix series' plot, cast, and release date have not yet been announced, its development is confirmed. Fans can look forward to more information as the creative process unfolds, with Blizzard and Netflix collaborating to bring Sanctuary's horrors to a new medium.

Yesterday, Blizzard president Johanna Faries revealed that a Diablo animated series is in the works but admitted she “can’t spill the beans” just yet on exactly what the new show entails. Regardless, the development team behind Diablo 4 says it’s quite possibly the reveal they are most excited about, even more so than the news that Diablo 5 is coming out in 2029 , Diablo 4 is getting a Switch 2 port, Spawn is coming to Diablo Immortal, and the arrival of the Amazon class. I sat down with Brent Gibson, Diablo 4’s Game Director, and Owen Leach, Season Lead for Diablo 4 - Hell’s Legacy, after yesterday’s news to break everything down. “Even though I have no information and can't share anything, the fact that we're getting a show [is what I’m most excited about]," Gibson says. “I'm a story guy. I want to see more story, as much story as you can get. We’re narrowing in on finding the creative team [for the show] and we're delivering on what Johanna was saying, [that] we're Blizzard Entertainment. I think Diablo's a perfect world to start telling those stories, so I couldn't be more happy that we're getting a show.” During yesterday’s presentation, Faries also noted that Overwatch, Warcraft and “perhaps even some…other [Blizzard] universes” could get their own series. But for now, news of a Diablo adaptation is proving to be more than enough to keep the development teams buzzing. “The show is my fan answer [for what I’m most excited about],” Leach says. “I've seen animated shows on Netflix and I'm like, ‘Hell yes.’" “I think this world of IPs existing and multiple media is the Wild West,” Gibson adds. “You actually can't predict how those mechanisms work. You watch other games that have gotten their shows and how that's plussed things up and changed things. Fallout is a really great example of that. You see this massive resurgence in the game because of the show and I love that.
